content: 1. Azithromycin can increase the levels or effects of cetirizine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 2. Chloroquine and azithromycin both increase the risk of QTc interval prolongation, which can lead to cardiac toxicity. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is essential. 3. Chlorpromazine and azithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Alternative medications should be considered due to the serious risk of cardiac complications. 4. Azithromycin may antagonize the effects of the cholera vaccine, reducing its efficacy. Systemic antibiotics, including azithromycin, should not be administered within 14 days prior to cholera vaccination. 5. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of ciprofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Alternative therapies should be considered, and close monitoring is necessary. 6. Azithromycin significantly increases the toxicity of cisapride by prolonging the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 7. Azithromycin and citalopram both prolong the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended, and caution should be exercised when co-administering these drugs. 8. Azithromycin and clarithromycin both increase the QTc interval. Close monitoring is required when these drugs are used together. 9. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of clofazimine by prolonging the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. 10. Clomipramine and azithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Alternative medications should be used due to the serious risk of cardiac complications. 11. Clozapine and azithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Additionally, azithromycin may increase clozapine toxicity through an unspecified mechanism. Alternative therapies are recommended. 12. Azithromycin and cobicistat can increase each other's levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative antibiotics should be considered when cobicistat is co-administered with atazanavir or darunavir. 13. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. If necessary, the colchicine dose should be reduced. 14. Azithromycin may decrease the effectiveness of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone, but the risk of contraceptive failure is low. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 15. Crizotinib and azithromycin both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac toxicity. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 16. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Close monitoring is required. 17. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of dabigatran by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided in patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment). 18. Azithromycin increases the effects of dalteparin by decreasing its metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 19. Azithromycin and dasatinib both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 20. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of degarelix by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 21. Azithromycin and desflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Alternative drugs should be used. 22. Azithromycin and desipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring is recommended. 23. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of deutetrabenazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Although the QTc prolongation is not clinically significant at the maximum recommended dose, certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. 24. Azithromycin and dichlorphenamide both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 25. Azithromycin decreases the effects of dicloxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 26. Azithromycin may decrease the effectiveness of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone, but the risk of contraceptive failure is low. Additional contraceptive methods may be advisable. 27. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 28. Azithromycin and disopyramide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 29. Azithromycin and dofetilide both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the serious risk of cardiac toxicity. 30. Azithromycin and dolasetron both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 31. Azithromycin and donepezil both prolong the QTc interval. Alternative drugs should be used. 32. Azithromycin and doxepin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 33. Azithromycin and dronedarone both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the increased risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. 34. Azithromycin and droperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 35. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Close monitoring is required. 36. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Dose adjustments may be required when co-administered with strong P-gp inhibitors. 37. Azithromycin and efavirenz both prolong the QTc interval. Alternative drugs should be used. 38. Azithromycin and eliglustat both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. 39. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of encorafenib by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 40.
